reason: I'll mount the motor in its cradle first to prepare the powered drive.
expectation: I expect a supported motor assembly, though it may still need fitting to the base.

alternatives.reason: The cord posts also seem necessary, but I want to prepare the motor first.

effect: The motor is secured and ready for a later fitting; I'll prepare the cord supports now.
reaction: A straightforward preparation, with no surprise.
reason: The cord posts are the only offered combination and should support the cord on the base.
expectation: I expect the posts and tension screw to be fitted to the base, ready for the cord.

effect: The posts are on the base, allowing the motor assembly to be fitted next.
reason: Fitting the motor to the base is the only offered combination and advances the powered drive.
expectation: I expect the cradled motor to be mounted on the base, ready for further drive parts.

effect: The motor is mounted on the wave frame; the eccentric driver is the next available fitting.
reason: The eccentric driver is the only offered combination and should help turn the motor's rotation into a wiggle.
expectation: I expect the driver to be fitted to the frame, though it may still need a belt to connect it to the motor.

effect: The off-centre peg will move in a circle to disturb one end of the cord; the belt should connect the drive.
reaction: The explanation makes the driver's purpose clearer.
reason: The belt is the only offered combination and should link the motor to the driver.
expectation: I expect the belt to transfer the motor's rotation to the eccentric driver.

effect: The belt drive is assembled, so the cord can now be added.
reason: The cord is the only offered combination and is needed to make the wave.
expectation: I expect the cord to be fitted between the posts and connected to the driver.

effect: The cord is fitted but loose, so it needs tension before the machine is ready.
reaction: The loose cord makes the next fitting's purpose clear.
reason: The tension spring is the only offered combination and should help keep the cord taut.
expectation: I expect the spring to tension the cord, though the drive may still need its guard.

effect: The cord is now tensioned; the drive guard remains to be fitted.
reaction: The spring did what I expected.
reason: The guard is the only offered combination and should cover the moving drive.
expectation: I expect a guarded wave machine that can shake the cord, though it may still need testing.

effect: The guard completes the drive while leaving its motion visible; the motor still needs a controller before it can run.
reaction: The clear guard is a useful detail, though I was curious to see the cord move.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the eccentric driver was most worthwhile: its off-centre peg gave a clear explanation of how rotation will disturb the cord.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the motor and then adding the belt felt like straightforward assembly without much to consider or learn.

surprise.text: I expected the guarded machine might be ready to test, so it was a surprise that the motor remains disconnected until a controller arrives.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, but most were the only offered combination, so there was little meaningful choice in their order.

continue.text: I would continue to see the cord actually move and learn what patterns the machine makes; the eccentric driver explanation made me curious, even though much of the assembly was routine.
